title: Can We Detect Sycophancy Before a Model Even Speaks?
epistemicStatus: Course project with honest null-ish results and one genuinely interesting signal. We found something, but it is modest, and we are saying so clearly.
excerpt: We adapted SYCON-Bench into a true multi-turn pressure benchmark with monotonically escalating disagreement, ran five open-weight LLMs through it, and asked whether hidden states at T0 already predict which questions a model will cave on. Zero-shot cosine similarity hits AUC 0.596–0.636. Linear probes fail entirely. The pre-flip signal is real, modest, and nonlinearly encoded. Paper submitted to EMNLP 2026.

title: The Scout-Refiner Bottleneck: A Negative Result with a Surprising Twist
epistemicStatus: Negative results from a small-scale (~125M param) experiment. The architecture is genuinely novel; none of that helped.
excerpt: I designed a two-stage attention module with a width bottleneck, expecting it to be more parameter-efficient than standard MHA. At equal token budget, the baseline beats every variant by 0.19–0.31 nats. But there's a crossover: at short training budgets, one variant actually wins.
